_note: Run: python3 bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/step3-plan.json (pure stdlib, no venv needed). Proves the Step-3 plan guards in tests/test_step3_plan.py are not vacuous: a lying checkbox, a mispointed `next`, a bumped ceiling, a new out-of-order port, a dropped/overlapping partition entry, a duplicate order, and an eval adapter ordered before the backbone it depends on are each caught. The mutations edit the machine-readable JSON block in docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md.

targets.label: a done method is marked done although its adapter is absent
the next pointer skips ahead past an earlier unfinished item
a deferred item drops its recorded reason (a silent skip)
the out-of-order ceiling is quietly widened in the plan
a new method is marked done ahead of its turn, exceeding the (now zero) ceiling
an unnumbered directory is dropped from the partition
a directory is listed as both a Step-3 port and a non-Step-3 exception
two items share an order (the ascending-order guard)
an eval adapter is pointed at a backbone ordered after it (adapter before its input)
